stimulus.text: From the Great Awakening through the period leading up to independence, Protestant evangelical ministers spoke of “liberty” and “virtue” delivering their congregants from “bondage and servitude.” The Boston Baptist minister John Allen's Oration Upon the Beauties of Liberty (1772), answering the Gaspee affair, was reprinted seven times in four cities. Evangelicals and republicans increasingly shared a language of opposition and resistance, likening British rule to the devil and urging colonists to resist corruption.
stimulus.source_note: Original secondary passage written for this question; the account follows Barron's Premium 2027, Chapter 5.

books.section: A. Protestant Evangelicalism and Enlightenment Philosophy

stem: How did Protestant evangelical preaching support the Patriot cause?

options.text: By teaching colonists that kings rule by divine right and must be obeyed
options.misconception: Divine right defends kings. Evangelical preaching likened British rule to the devil, not to God's order.

options.text: By ordering congregations to stay out of politics entirely
options.misconception: The ministers did the opposite — they preached resistance and carried liberty into the pulpit.

options.text: By giving resistance a language of liberty against bondage and tyranny
By arguing that only the wealthy should take part in public life
options.misconception: The passage says nothing about wealth. Evangelical preaching spoke to congregants of all stations about liberty.

rationales.C: Ministers spoke of liberty and virtue delivering people from bondage and servitude, and likened British rule to the devil. The pulpit gave the Patriots a moral language everyone already knew.
rationales.A: Divine right would defend the king. Evangelical preaching attacked British rule as godless tyranny.
rationales.B: Staying out of politics is the opposite of what the passage describes — ministers preached resistance from the pulpit.
rationales.D: Wealth is not in the passage. The preaching reached whole congregations with a language of liberty.
rationales.general:
1. Listen to the ministers' words. Liberty and virtue delivering congregants from bondage and servitude.
2. Hear the comparison. British rule likened to the devil, the struggle cast as godless tyranny.
3. Name the gift. Preaching gave the resistance a moral language ordinary colonists already knew.
Remember: ideas move people when they arrive in words people already use — the pulpit gave the Patriots their vocabulary.
